tier1.text: T tubules carry electrical signals from a muscle cell's surface to the inside of the cell. Each T tubule is an inward fold of the cell's outer membrane. Inside, the signal makes the nearby sarcoplasmic reticulum, the cell's calcium store, release calcium. This calcium starts the cell's contraction.

sentences.text: T tubules carry electrical signals from a muscle cell's surface to the inside of the cell.

quotes.quote: T (transverse) tubules penetrate from the surface plasma membrane, the sarcolemma, to the interior of the cell, allowing the electrical impulse to reach the interior.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Each T tubule is an inward fold of the cell's outer membrane.

quotes.quote: Invagination of the plasma membrane of a muscle cell that extends inward from the cell surface around each myofibril.

sentences.text: Inside, the signal makes the nearby sarcoplasmic reticulum, the cell's calcium store, release calcium.

quotes.quote: The T-tubules carry the action potential into the interior of the cell, which triggers the opening of calcium channels in the membrane of the adjacent SR, causing Ca++ to diffuse out of the SR and into the sarcoplasm.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: In muscle cells, a specialized SER, the sarcoplasmic reticulum, is responsible for storing calcium ions that are needed to trigger the muscle cells' coordinated contractions.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: This calcium starts the cell's contraction.

quotes.quote: It is the arrival of Ca++ in the sarcoplasm that initiates contraction of the muscle fiber by its contractile units, or sarcomeres.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
